Materion.why: Its Electronic Materials segment supplies sputtering targets and PVD materials for leading-edge logic and memory chips; AI chip demand drives its semiconductor sales (+23%) and orders
Materion.evidence: Materion Q2 FY2026 (08-05-2026): CFO - Electronic Materials value-added sales up 15% 'driven by continued strength in semiconductor as AI adoption fuels high demand for semiconductor chips'; CEO - semiconductor sales up 23% on leading-edge logic and memory

players.product: High-purity sputtering targets, evaporation materials and PVD consumables (backing plates, crucible liners) for leading-edge logic, memory (incl. HBM) and data storage

quarterly_data.signal: Record value-added sales of $308.2 million, up 15% year-over-year and 18% sequentially; adjusted EBITDA a record $71.8 million (23.3% of value-added sales); adjusted EPS a record $1.90, up 39% (CFO).

Electronic Materials value-added sales were $87.4 million, up 15% year-over-year, driven by semiconductor as AI adoption fuels demand for chips and data storage devices plus new business wins; record adjusted EBITDA of $28 million (32% of value-added sales), up 57%, the fifth consecutive quarter of margin expansion (CFO). CEO: sales to the semiconductor market were up 23% year-over-year as AI drives growth across leading-edge logic and memory.

CEO: record backlog up roughly 30% from last year and 20% since the start of the year; first-half incoming orders reached a new high, up nearly 30% year-over-year; semiconductor orders are up 20% with a meaningful uptick in demand for high-performance memory applications; telecom and data center sales grew almost 50% on the AI infrastructure build-out.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog +30% YoY; semiconductor orders +20%; telecom and data center almost 50%

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance raised for the second consecutive quarter: mid-teens 2026 sales growth and adjusted EPS of $6.80-$7.20 (prior $6-$6.50), roughly 30% above last year at the midpoint; CFO expects additional Electronic Materials top-line improvement from rising semiconductor demand and new business.

CFO: Q2 Electronic Materials mix was probably richer than will be seen all year, but margins will structurally be well ahead of last year. CEO: Materion supplies across power semi, communications, data storage, logic, memory and high bandwidth memory, and believes its orders are for consumption within roughly six to nine months, not inventory buildup.

CEO: capacity is well-positioned to support the growth coming in the next year, funded where possible by customers and government; CFO: Materion was awarded a $65 million investment from one of the primes to expand beryllium capacity, not shown in the CapEx forecast.

CEO: defense incoming orders were $90 million in the first half with more than $500 million of open RFQs (around $300 million last quarter); space orders doubled year-over-year and the space business has grown six times in three to four years (about 25% of aerospace and defense); a new $15 million program was secured for engine materials for a major commercial space customer. Performance Materials value-added sales $190 million (+13%); Precision Optics $30.8 million (+26%) (CFO).
quarterly_data.figure: $90 million orders; $500 million RFQs; $15 million program
